answer: Copying the same citations across 158 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 158 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the trellis index resolves every citation against the zephyr checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the jetty audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 22 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
